analysis.title: The Last Safe Haven Reports: Everything You Need To Know Ahead Of Apple Earnings
key_insights: Apple reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company on Friday, and its correlation to the Nasdaq 100 turned negative for the first time ever. Apple is up 17% since the end of June while the Nasdaq 100 is down 6%, including a 7.4% drop after the China and Services miss on July 30.

The Street expects fiscal Q4 (September quarter) revenue of $113.5B, at the top of Apple's $111.7-113.7B guidance range, with EPS of $2.00 and gross margin of 47.6% (guidance 47-48%). iPhone is expected at $56.5B and Services at $31.6B per Bloomberg.

Sell-side has converged on in-line results. UBS's Vogt (Neutral, $296 PT) is slightly below consensus at $112.8B revenue and $56.0B iPhone, reflecting about 5% fewer units offset by about 5% higher ASPs. Goldman's Ng (Buy, $390 PT) expects iPhone +15% y/y and Services +10% y/y. JPMorgan's Chatterjee has revenue at $112.9B (+10% y/y).

The December-quarter guide matters more than the print. Goldman expects Apple to guide total revenue growth of LSD%-MSD% y/y. JPMorgan models December-quarter revenue of $147.9B (+3% y/y) with iPhone revenue of $84.0B (-2% y/y) on 69mm units (-18% y/y).

Early reads on iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max demand are weak after a $100 price increase: Bernstein found US demand down low single digits y/y (China +12% in launch week), Nikkei reported October component orders for the two Pro models cut 15-20%, and Loop Capital downgraded to Hold on Oct 20 on shipment reductions.

The iPhone Duo (about $2,000 foldable) had display cracking problems. Apple acknowledged display problems and offered replacements. UBS Evidence Lab had average Duo wait times at 89 days as of last week.

Gross margin estimates include a roughly 100bp one-off tariff-refund benefit (UBS 47.5%, Goldman 47.8%). Excluding it, UBS expects gross margin to decline largely on higher DRAM costs. South Korean DRAM exports hit a record $34B in October, up 595% y/y, and TrendForce sees mobile DRAM contract prices up 0-5% q/q in Q4.

Services growth is expected at about +10% y/y ($31.6B) after a July miss of almost $1B at 12% growth. UBS notes App Store growth slowed to low single digits. Goldman's Callahan asks whether Apple can hold double-digit growth on this line.
Apple enters earnings at an all-time high multiple of 36x forward P/E, a 17x premium to the S&P 500 per Goldman's Callahan, against an S&P forward P/E of 18.4x.

Positioning is split. Nomura's McElligott flagged massive upside vol buying in megacap tech into earnings with Apple leading. Bear Traps Report said it is long AAPD (inverse Apple ETF) with high conviction.

The Wednesday at-the-money straddle implies about 4.4%, roughly double Apple's 2.3% average absolute move over the past 12 reports. The expiry also covers Tuesday's midterms, but Goldman's Garrett notes index-level excess variance for the midterms is nonexistent. Apple fell 7.3% on its last report.
This is John Ternus' first earnings call as CEO. Goldman's Esposito calls it the ultimate test for consumer hardware elasticity and self-funded AI deployment.
Deutsche Bank strategists flipped back to positive on US tech after an 11% drawdown. The article notes that if AI names bounce, haven money has somewhere else to go.

market_movers.rationale: UBS's Vogt made limited estimate changes ahead of earnings and sits slightly below consensus at $112.8B revenue and EPS of $1.97. He notes an opex-driven beat is unlikely to be rewarded.
Goldman's Ng expects in-line F4Q26 results with iPhone +15% y/y on price increases and Services +10% y/y, and sees FY27 supported by price increases and a replacement cycle.
Loop Capital downgraded to Hold on Oct 20, citing iPhone shipment reductions.
JPMorgan's Chatterjee has fiscal Q4 revenue at $112.9B (+10% y/y) and FY27 revenue of $518.3B (+9%), just below consensus, on about 247 million iPhone units (+3%).
The Bear Traps Report told clients it is long AAPD, the inverse Apple ETF, with high conviction ahead of earnings.

sector_views.rationale: Deutsche Bank strategists flipped back to positive on US tech after an 11% drawdown.

earnings_insights: Apple fiscal Q4 (September quarter) consensus per Bloomberg: revenue $113.5B (guidance $111.7-113.7B), EPS $2.00 consensus est, gross margin 47.6% (guidance 47-48%), iPhone $56.5B and Services $31.6B. Reports Monday Nov 2 after the close.

UBS Vogt estimate for F4Q26: total revenue $112.8B vs consensus $113.6B, iPhone $56.0B vs consensus $56.2B, EPS $1.97 vs $1.99 consensus est. iPhone expected to grow close to 14% y/y. Gross margin 47.5% includes about 100bp tariff-refund benefit.
Goldman Ng F4Q26 estimate: iPhone +15% y/y, Services +10% y/y, gross margin 47.8% including a 1pp tariff-refund benefit. His growth rates work out to about $56.4B iPhone and $31.6B Services.

JPMorgan Chatterjee F4Q26 estimate: revenue $112.9B (+10% y/y), modestly above the guidance midpoint. December-quarter estimate: revenue $147.9B (+3% y/y), iPhone revenue $84.0B (-2% y/y), 69mm units (-18% y/y). FY27 revenue $518.3B (+9%), iPhone units about 247 million (+3%).
Goldman expects Apple to guide December-quarter total revenue growth of LSD%-MSD% y/y. JPMorgan also expects low to mid-single digit growth with iPhone ASPs offsetting lower volumes.
The prior report on July 30 was a China and Services miss. Services grew 12%, missing by almost $1B, and the stock fell 7.3% to 7.4% on the print.

macro_indicators.interpretation: All-time high absolute multiple and a 17x premium to the S&P 500, leaving little room for a disappointing guide.
Apple's forward P/E is nearly double the index multiple.
Record memory export value points to sharply higher DRAM costs for hardware makers such as Apple.
TrendForce expects further memory cost increases, which pressures Apple's margins after the tariff refund fades.

trade_ideas.description: Long AAPD (inverse Apple ETF) into Apple earnings
trade_ideas.rationale: Bear Traps Report cites Apple's record 36x forward P/E and expected unit declines.

risk_factors: Price-volume elasticity: iPhone units expected down 18% y/y in the December quarter with price doing the work.
Memory cost inflation pressures gross margin once the tariff refund benefit of about 100bp is removed.
Services growth slowing, with App Store growth at low single digits and regulatory pressure on App Store monetization.
Record 36x forward P/E leaves the stock exposed to multiple contraction.
Duo display problems and potential buyer deferral to a second-generation foldable or the Pro models.
An opex-driven EPS beat is unlikely to be rewarded by investors per UBS.
vol_and_positioning: The Wednesday at-the-money AAPL straddle implies about 4.4%, versus a 2.3% average absolute move over the past 12 reports.

Goldman's Garrett notes excess variance for the midterms at the index level remains nonexistent. The Wednesday SPX straddle captures Apple earnings and midterms yet costs 30bps less than Friday's single session move.
Nomura's McElligott flagged massive upside vol buyers in megacap tech into earnings, with Apple leading, on Monday and Tuesday of last week.
UBS Sales & Trading sentiment score on Apple is 6.5 out of 10, versus 9 for Amazon the prior week.
Apple's correlation to the Nasdaq 100 turned negative for the first time ever.
Bear Traps Report is long AAPD (inverse Apple ETF), high conviction.
geopolitical: Tuesday's US midterm elections fall inside the Wednesday option expiry that also covers Apple earnings.
Tariff refunds are providing a one-off gross margin benefit of about 100bp to Apple.
Apple's China iPhone demand: Bernstein found China Pro and Pro Max demand up 12% in launch week.
cross_bank_references: Goldman, UBS and JPMorgan all converge on in-line fiscal Q4 results.
Nomura's McElligott flagged upside vol buyers while Bear Traps Report is long AAPD.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Ng expects in-line results and sees FY27 supported by iPhone price increases, a Duo-driven replacement cycle and spring 2027 launches. Nomura's McElligott flagged upside vol buyers in megacap tech with Apple leading.
tension_points.bear_case: Apple trades at a record 36x forward P/E while JPMorgan sees December-quarter iPhone units down 18% y/y, margin is helped by a one-off tariff refund, and Services growth is slowing. The Bear Traps Report is long AAPD.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A December-quarter guide at the high end of LSD-MSD% revenue growth would undercut the bear case, while an opex-driven beat without a strong guide would not be rewarded.

theme_stances.key_argument: A 36x multiple is a lot to pay for fewer phones at higher prices, and an opex beat will not cover for that.
theme_stances.evidence: a 36x multiple is a lot to pay for fewer phones at higher prices
